picked.body: Mainland China and Hong Kong accounted for the biggest share of shipments, worth $1.42 billion, according to the Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Producers. Exports to the U.S. were worth over $563 million, followed by Japan with $503 million, the EU with $461 million and Australia with $241 million. Whiteleg shrimp exports amounted to $2.62 billion while green lobster and black tiger shrimp generated $915 million and $407.2 million, respectively. The association said the global shrimp market is projected to see abundant supplies from Ecuador and India next year, intensifying price competition. Demand is expected to vary across markets and segments while trade will be affected by tariff policies and import barriers, it noted. Value-added, convenient and premium shrimp products are becoming increasingly important while production costs, traceability and sustainability are emerging as key factors determining competitiveness, it added. Roughly 759,500 hectares are used for shrimp farming across Vietnam, including 637,400 hectares for black tiger shrimp and 122,100 hectares for whiteleg shrimp, according to official reports. Production is estimated to jump 5% year-on-year to 1.47 million tonnes this year, with whiteleg shrimp accounting for 69% and black tiger shrimp the remainder. The target output for next year is 1.5 million tonnes. The Mekong Delta is the top producer, accounting for 94% of area and 88% of nationwide output. Vietnam currently has 488 shrimp-processing facilities that qualify for export with a combined designed capacity of around 1.4 million tonnes a year. The industry faces several challenges, including fragmented production, inadequate infrastructure in farming areas and a lack of consistent controls over the quality and traceability of shrimp seed. Data on environmental monitoring, disease outbreaks and production are not effectively integrated while cooperation among farmers, cooperatives and businesses remains weak. The Department of Fisheries and Fisheries Surveillance pointed out that higher production does not necessarily translate into higher profits and incomes for farmers. The ability to coordinate and manage the entire value chain, from shrimp seed and farming conditions to purchasing, processing and distribution, also needs improvement, it said.

picked.t: Where most international students study in the US
picked.body: The Institute of International Education (IIE) released its annual Open Doors report in mid-November, reporting more than 1.14 million international students in the United States during the 2025–2026 academic year. Their spending contributed approximately US$56 billion to the U.S. economy. By state, New York and California lead the country, each hosting more than 130,000 and being the only states where the number of foreign students exceed 100,000. The Midwest has the largest representation among the top 10 states, with four entries, followed by the Northeast with three. However, studying in these popular destinations can come at a high cost. The College Board estimates that international students may need between $28,200 and $50,000 for living expenses during the upcoming academic year, depending on their location. Major metropolitan areas in New York, California, Massachusetts and Pennsylvania are among the most expensive. Among individual institutions, NYU ranks first, with 26,600 international students. California has four universities among the top 15, including three campuses in the University of California system. New York and Massachusetts each account for two institutions on the list. For the 2026–2027 academic year, annual tuition at the universities featured in the ranking ranges from $24,900 to $75,300. The University of North Texas has the lowest tuition, while NYU charges the highest. The Open Doors report recorded approximately 27,300 Vietnamese students in the United States during the previous academic year, making Vietnam the sixth-largest source country of international students. Vietnamese students were most concentrated in Texas, California, Washington, Massachusetts and Florida.

picked.t: Singapore's Apartment Coffee named best cafe in Asia-Pacific
picked.body: The new ranking, announced last week at the World Coffee Forum in Seoul, South Korea, was created by the team behind The World's 100 Best Coffee Shops, a well-known global awards platform that celebrates top specialty coffee destinations. Apartment Coffee finished ahead of second-place Only Coffee Project Crows Nest in Sydney, Australia, and third-place Ult Coffee in Osaka, Japan. Founded in 2018 by award-winning barista Yeo Qing He, the Singapore cafe is famous for its carefully sourced single-origin beans and hand-brewed pour-over coffee. According to Singaporean news channel CNA , the cafe ranked sixth in the world for two years in a row before winning this top regional title. Five other Singaporean cafes made the list: Alchemist (36th), Homeground Coffee Roasters (38th), The Community Coffee (50th), Cata Coffee (55th), and The Populus (90th). Story of Ono in Petaling Jaya, Malaysia took fourth place and Omakafé in Jakarta, Indonesia was seventh. Both countries secured five spots in the ranking. The Philippines matched Singapore with six featured cafes, led by Yardstick in Makati at number 23. Thailand and Vietnam followed with three entries each. Thailand's highest-ranked cafe was Fika & Co. Cafe in Bangkok at number 25, while Vietnam's top entry was Lacàph Coffee Experiences Space in Ho Chi Minh City at number 29. In all, 28 Southeast Asian cafes made the list. To choose the winners, the organizers combined public votes with scores from a panel of coffee experts. Public voting made up 30% of the final score and experienced baristas, roasters, and industry professionals accounted for the rest. This expert panel judged each cafe on eight key criteria: coffee quality, barista skill, customer service, innovations, atmosphere, eco-friendly practices, food quality, and community spirit.
